long_biography.plain_text:
Jerry Richardson made the Carolina Panthers the culmination of a life shaped by football in the Carolinas. A standout receiver at Wofford College, he later caught a touchdown from Johnny Unitas in the 1959 NFL Championship Game during two seasons with the Baltimore Colts. Decades later, he led Charlotte's successful campaign for an expansion franchise, awarded in 1993.

Richardson's ownership group pioneered permanent seat licences to help finance the stadium privately, and the Panthers reached the conference championship in their second season. He maintained a close association with Wofford, where the team held training camp, and gave more than a quarter of a billion dollars to the college. His donations supported scholarships, academic buildings and athletic facilities across the campus.
